source_text: Unam ergo saltem contra tantam a nobis productorum testium dignitatem, contra iustitiam manifestam, contra perspicuam rationem legis ede sententiam, per quam te ostendas fuisse deceptum; quod ideo addidi, quia, etiamsi esset, quae tale aliquid ambiguitate verborum putaretur ostendere, aliarum tamen sententiarum splendore et magisterio ita, ut iustitiae congruebat, cogebatur exponi.
pass_a_gloss: Produce therefore at least one sentence of the law against so great a dignity of witnesses produced by us, against manifest justice, against the clear reason of the law, through which you may show you were deceived; which I have added for this reason, because even if there were one which by ambiguity of words might be thought to show such a thing, nevertheless by the splendor and teaching of other sentences it was forced to be exposed as justice was fitting.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Produce, then, at least one pronouncement of the law against the great authority of the witnesses we have brought forward, against manifest justice and clear reason—a pronouncement through which you can show you were deceived. I add that last phrase because even if some passage seemed, through ambiguous wording, to indicate such a thing, the brilliance and teaching of other pronouncements would compel it to be explained in a way consistent with justice.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
